sections.h2: How Do Saudi Buyers Search for Suppliers?
sections.intro: Understanding search behaviour in the Kingdom is what makes Saudi SEO different from SEO in other markets:

items.html: Mobile first: most searches happen on phones, so speed and simple layouts matter more than design extras.
Arabic and English mixed: consumers often search in Arabic, while B2B buyers and expatriates often search in English. Many people use both.
Google Maps for local services: "near me" searches for clinics, restaurants and contractors are common in every major city.
Trust signals: a Saudi phone number, a clear Commercial Registration mention, prices in SAR and reviews from local customers increase enquiries.

items.title: SEO for Saudi B2B Companies
items.text: SEO for Saudi B2B companies targets procurement and technical searches, such as supplier names, product specifications and "company in Riyadh" terms. We build service pages, case studies and downloadable profiles that sales teams can share.

items.title: SEO Services for Saudi Ecommerce Stores
items.html: SEO services for Saudi ecommerce stores cover category pages, product schema, Arabic product titles, fast mobile checkout and visible delivery and return details. If you need a new site first, see our web design company in Saudi Arabia page.

items.title: SEO for Companies Entering the Saudi Market
items.text: SEO for companies entering the Saudi market starts with research: which cities to target first, what buyers search for in each language, and which local competitors already rank. This helps you plan your launch before spending on ads.

sections.h2: Tracking With Consent Under Saudi PDPL

paragraphs.html: Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL) has applied in full since September 2024 and is overseen by the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA). For SEO, this mainly affects how your website tracks visitors and collects form data. We set up Google Analytics 4 with a clear consent banner, a plain privacy notice and lead forms that only ask for what you need. This keeps your reports accurate and your website aligned with the law. See the official guidance from SDAIA. We are not lawyers, so we recommend your legal adviser reviews your privacy notice.
